attribution_limitations: Diuretics are said to be discontinued after four weeks, but the patient was discharged at the age of 25 days and the therapy was discontinued before discharge. Four weeks (28 days) exceeds 25 days; an arithmetic-only mismatch, not a source conflict. Neither is corrected.

The fistula closures ("One was closed with Histoacryl glue and the two others with coils") and the ductus closure ("Additionally, the patent ductus arteriosus was closed") carry no time of their own and are not stated to be part of the fourth procedure; they are kept untimed. The fistula closure is ordered after the fourth-procedure angiography only because it acts on the fistulas that angiography revealed; the ductus closure is ordered after the open ductus finding and the Figure 8A aortography.

The aortic arch, left subclavian artery, retrograde diastolic flow and open ductus findings are in a paragraph that does not name the modality or time; they are kept in their own event and not assigned to echocardiography. The Figure 1 caption separately states echocardiography after birth showing a dilated left subclavian artery (recorded as its own caption finding); neither is merged with the CT angiography diameter.
The text says "cardiac CT was assigned" and later reports a "multislice CT angiography scan"; the source does not state they are the same study.
Upper arm size is called "circumference" in the first measurements and "diameter" after the fourth procedure (21 cm vs 16 cm). Same measurement type is not stated; both wordings are kept as printed.

The text names fistulas between the left subclavian artery and left cephalic vein during the fourth procedure and cites Figures 5 and 6; the Figure 6 caption names the cephalic and basilic veins and states no time. The Figure 6 finding is kept as its own untimed event.
One of the two parents carries the same variant; the source does not say whether it is the mother or the father.

The Discussion contains general statements about Parkes Weber syndrome, imaging and treatment; they are literature or review statements and are not copied to the patient. The stated "first patient with genetically confirmed PWS in Latvia" is a study limitation, not a patient fact.

The text places the selective angiography of the descending aorta and left subclavian artery during the fourth procedure, while the Figure 5 caption calls it descending aorta angiography before the fourth procedure. Each finding keeps its own stated time; they are not merged.

The Figure 7B caption shows AV fistulas closed with detachable coils; the text says detachable micro-coils were used in the first three embolisations and that two fistulas were closed with coils after the fourth-procedure angiography. The source does not identify which procedure Figure 7 shows, so the caption closure is kept separate and untimed.
